name: Najib Mikati
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Najib Mikati cofounded Beirut-based investment firm M1 Group.
Mikati currently served as the prime minister of Lebanon until February 2025, a position he previously held from 2011 to 2014 and briefly in 2005.
Mikati and his billionaire brother Taha founded Investcom in 1982, selling satellite phones at the height of Lebanon's civil war.
They expanded into Africa where they built cellphone towers in Ghana, Liberia and Benin, among other countries.
In 2005, Investcom went public on the London Stock Exchange, and in 2009, South Africa's MTN bought the Mikatis' stake for $3.6 billion.
forbes_facts: In 2005, Investcom was the largest IPO of a Middle Eastern company in London, and the first stock to trade on the Dubai Financial Market.

name: Barry Zekelman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Barry Zekelman took over his family's steel business at age 19 and has since grown it into one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.
He sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but continued to help run it. He and his family bought it back in 2011.
Today Barry and his two brothers, Clayton and Alan Zekelman, split 100% ownership of the $3.3 billion (revenues) firm, now named Zekelman Industries.
The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.
forbes_facts: One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona.
Zekelman races Ferraris and has owned a series of yachts named "Man of Steel."

name: Fang Wei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Fang Wei chairs Fangda Group, a conglomerate based in the northeastern province of Liaoning with interests in aviation, pharmaceuticals, steel and new materials.
The group controls several listed companies, including Fangda Carbon New Material and Fangda Special Steel Technology.
Born in a distressed rural area, Fang helped his family recycle scrap metals when he was young.
He later built a sprawling business empire through acquiring financially stressed companies and turning their operations around.

His best-known deals include the 2022 investment of  $1.6 billion in Hainan Airlines, after former owner HNA Group was forced to downsize amid Beijing's crackdown on debt-fueled acquisitions overseas.

name: John Krystynak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: John Krystynak cofounded AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin in 2012.
He served as AppLovin's chief technology officer until 2020 but left the company a year before its IPO in 2021.
He owned 4% of AppLovin as of December 2023, when he dropped below the SEC's disclosure threshold.
He is one of eight billionaires from AppLovin, including the company's cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.

name: Hu Rongda
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Hu Rongda is the founder of Zhejiang Sanmei Chemical Industry, a maker of fluorine chemical products; its refrigerant and HFCs refrigerants are used in home, auto and industrial air conditioning systems.
Hu Rongda shares his fortune with son Hu Qixiang, the company's chairman.
Sanmei went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: Jorge Perez
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Jorge Perez runs Miami-based real estate developer Related Group, which claims to have developed more than 100,000 condos and apartments since it was founded in 1979.
As a young urban planner, Perez met developer Stephen Ross, which led to a partnership. Ross' Related Companies held a 25% stake until 2022, when Perez bought it out.
They built affordable housing in the 1980s, then expanded to market-rate rental apartments and high-end condo construction in the 1990s.
Perez has started diversifying where he develops, branching out elsewhere in Florida as well as in Arizona, Georgia and North Carolina plus Brazil and Mexico.
forbes_facts: A son of Cuban parents, Perez grew up in Argentina and Colombia before moving to the U.S. for college.
In 2011 Perez donated $40 million in cash and artwork to the Miami Art Museum, which then agreed to rename it after him. Nicknamed PAMM, it opened in 2013.

name: Divya Gokulnath
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2020-2021); Hurun India (2019); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2023)
forbes_bio: A former math tutor, Byju Raveendran founded online ed-tech company Byju's in 2011.
The company's last funding round in November 2022 valued it at around $20 billion. Byju's investors include Mark Zuckerberg and Tencent.
Byju reported a net loss of 45.6 billion rupees ($573 million) for the year ended March 2021, compared to a loss of 3.1 billion rupees the previous year as operating expenses doubled,
His wife Divya, who was one of his early students, helps him run the company and also sits on the board.
forbes_facts: The company collects old and unused smart devices, loads them with Byju's content and distributes them to poor children.
Raveendran is an avid traveller and loves playing with numbers.

name: Aditya Khemka
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Aditya Khemka is the founder and managing director of Aditya Infotech, which provides security surveillance products like CCTVs and security cameras.
The Delhi-based company sells its products under the CP Plus brand.
Aditya Infotech has a wide range of offerings, from smart home IoT cameras to thermal cameras and AI solutions.
His father Hari Khemka is company chairman and the older of his two sons, Ananmay, has a board seat.
Khemka listed the company in August 2025 at a 50% premium to the issue price.

name: Raj Sardana
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Raj Sardana is the founder and CEO of Innova Solutions, an IT services firm based in Atlanta, Georgia.
A first-generation Indian immigrant, Sardana originally started the company, formerly named American CyberSystems, as a staffing firm that connected US companies with tech talent in India.
It has since expanded to help clients including Verizon, Centene and Change Healthcare with outsourcing technical projects.
Innova Solutions, which is owned by Sardana and his immediate family members, generated $2.4 billion in sales in 2022.
forbes_facts: Before starting Innova Solutions, Sardana, who has a master's in mechanical engineering, worked at a missile engine company and owned gas stations.
Sardana says he has top secret security clearance with the U.S. government because of his company's defense contracts.

name: Julio Mario Santo Domingo III
name_chinese: 朱利奥·马里奥·桑托·多明戈
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2015-2020); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Julio Mario Santo Domingo III, an heir to one of the world's largest beer fortunes, is a disc jockey in New York City for the group Sheik 'N' Beik.
He inherited his wealth from his late grandfather, who owned a large stake in SABMiller following its 2005 acquisition of family brewer Bavaria.
In 2016, Anheuser-Bush InBev acquired SABMiller for $100 billion.
Santo Domingo graduated from Boston University with a bachelor's degree in architecture; his stage name as a DJ is Rechulski.
In 2016, Santo Domingo launched Okeechobee Music & Arts Festival, a music festival held annually in Okeechobee, Florida.
forbes_facts: Santo Domingo's father's collection of memorabilia documenting psychoactive drugs is the world's largest and currently loaned to Harvard University.
His grandfather merged his beer company with Bavaria in the 1960s, eventually obtaining a 75% stake in the larger company.
